chunks: "First I'd figure out what kind of memory I'm short of, because the fix is different.
If it's program space, I'd check the compiler optimisation, drop unused libraries and maybe compress data.
If that's not enough, many parts can run code from external QSPI flash that's memory-mapped, or I move to the pin-compatible variant with more flash.
If it's RAM, I'd cut buffers, put big constant tables in flash, reuse buffers, and if I truly need more, add external SRAM or PSRAM, or step up to a part with more internal RAM.
If it's data storage, like logging, I'd add an external memory: an I2C or SPI EEPROM or flash for small amounts, an SD card for gigabytes, or FRAM when I need endless writes.
I'd choose by capacity, speed and how many pins I can spare. For example, a 1 kilohertz, 16-bit logger makes 2 kB per second, about 7 MB per hour.
That fits easily on a 16 MB SPI flash for two hours, and an SD card holds days. A plain SPI bus at 10 megahertz moves 1.
25 MB per second, hundreds of times more than I need, so the bus isn't the constraint. Capacity and flash wear are."
